title: Ten Songs to Remember Valentín Elizalde 20 Years After His Passing
summary: "Vete Ya," "Cómo Me Duele" and other iconic tracks that defined Elizalde's legacy as "El Gallo de Oro."
body: This Wednesday (Nov. 25) marks 20 years since the assassination of Valentín Elizalde , the regional Mexican singer who, at the height of his career, was gunned down after a performance in Reynosa, in northern Mexico, along with his manager Mario Mendoza and his driver Reynaldo Ballesteros. To this day, the reasons or culprits behind the crime remain unknown. At just 27 years old, the singer from Sonora was already an icon, thanks to his commanding personality and unique interpretive style, accompanied by Sinaloan banda music. Despite not possessing a powerful voice, Elizalde poured emotion into songs like “Vete Ya,” “Cómo Me Duele,” “Vencedor” and “Te Quiero Así,” which have become timeless classics in Mexican music. Related 20 Years Without Valentín Elizalde: Makers of New Docuseries Discuss the Late Musical Icon & His Still-Unsolved Murder During his lifetime, “El Gallo de Oro” (The Golden Rooster), as he was known, entered the top 10 of Billboard ‘s Regional Mexican Airplay chart in 2003 with his hit “Vete Ya.” After his death, his album Vencedor , which had been released months earlier, reached No. 1 on both Top Latin Albums and Top Regional Mexican …

title: Rauw Alejandro Is Fulfilling a Childhood Dream With Rockstar Games: ”GTA’ Has Been Part of My Life’
summary: Alejandro chats with Billboard about joining the GTA VI soundtrack and bringing throwback reggaetón energy to the game with “Macacoa 2000.”
body: Like many adults right now, Rauw Alejandro is probably glued to the couch playing Grand Theft Auto VI . Age is nothing but a number for millennials who grew up reveling in the criminal escapades and explosive gameplay Rockstar Games has offered gamers over the last two decades. Now, Rauw isn’t just reliving his childhood; he’s part of one of the biggest video games in history, thanks to his inclusion on the blockbuster soundtrack, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album . “When I heard about the opportunity, I was like, ‘Let’s gooo! We gotta bring that Puerto Rican underground sound to GTA y más que nuevamente regresa a Miami , home of many Latinos,’” he tells Billboard . “Growing up playing GTA , I never imagined I’d get to be part of its soundtrack. As a fan, it’s crazy to experience something like this. GTA has always been about the culture, and now getting to bring my own sound into that world is just insane. It’s a full-circle moment for me, de verdad . Something really special.” Alejandro’s electric track, “Macacoa 2000,” is a love letter to throwback reggaeton that complements the game’s Miami-inspired setting. title: YouTube Music could finally let you pin your favorite playlists and albums where they belong
summary: Spotify users have enjoyed library pinning for a while, and it looks like YouTube Music is finally catching up.
body: TL;DR YouTube Music is working on a new feature that could let users pin songs, albums, playlists, and artists directly to their Library for quicker access. The feature is separate from the existing Pin to Speed dial option, which only adds shortcuts to the Home tab. Spotify already offers Library pinning, but it’s unclear how Google’s implementation will work or when it will roll out. YouTube Music might finally be addressing one of those little annoyances that can make using a music streaming app more frustrating than it needs to be — having to hunt through your Library to find the music you listen to the most. We’ve spotted signs of a new pinning feature in the latest YouTube Music Android app (version 9.46.55), and it could let users pin their favorite songs, albums, and playlists directly to the Library tab, making frequently played music much easier to find.

title: Android Canary 2611 hides an iPhone-style scroll-to-top shortcut, and we got it working
summary: Google hasn't added a way to trigger it yet, but you can almost guess what gesture it would adopt for this shortcut.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Android Canary 2611 contains code for a system-wide scroll-to-top feature, similar to tapping the status bar on an iPhone. We managed to activate the feature ahead of its release. It worked in Settings and Gmail but not in apps built with Jetpack Compose, like the Play Store. Google hasn’t built the exact gesture for it or announced the feature yet, but AndroidX is already being updated to support it. Dormant code for the feature has also appeared in Samsung’s One UI 9.5 Beta 1 for the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Android phones handle system navigation much better than iPhones, in my opinion, but there’s still one area where iOS manages to eke past Android . If you’ve ever scrolled down a long list on Android, you’d notice you have to scroll or quick-flick your way back to the top. It’s a small gesture you probably don’t think much about, but on iPhones, you can simply tap the status bar to quickly glide straight back to the top. If you’ve ever wished Android could do the same, Google might just be answering your prayers with the new scroll-to-top feature. It’s the latest in a string of iPhone-style conveniences Google is working on, after Androi…

The phone also packs a 6,200mAh battery, a 50MP main camera with LOFIC tech, and support for up to four SIMs. HUAWEI has been subject to a US trade ban since 2019, but you wouldn’t know this based on its recent smartphone hardware. title: Samsung’s Tizen-based Galaxy Watch gets an unofficial Wear OS 3.5 port
summary: Eight years later, there's potentially more life in this old watch.
body: TL;DR A developer has released an unofficial Wear OS 3.5 port based on Android 11 for the original Samsung Galaxy Watch (SM-R800). The port uses Pixel Watch software and reportedly supports Gemini, the Play Store, GPS, and health tracking. The port and installation guide are available on GitHub, though it remains experimental. Samsung’s switch from Tizen to Wear OS in 2021 opened up a whole new world of apps and Google services for Galaxy Watch owners. But you needed a Galaxy Watch 4 or newer to enjoy those benefits. Older models were left behind, and as Samsung wound down its Tizen smartwatch ecosystem , their usefulness gradually diminished. However, one developer is giving the original Galaxy Watch another shot at life. A developer known as Depth118 has shared an unofficial Android 11-based Wear OS 3.5 port on GitHub for Samsung’s 2018 Galaxy Watch. The project uses software from the original Google Pixel Watch, which, despite launching four years later, shares the same Exynos 9110 processor. The port is specifically designed for the 46mm Bluetooth Galaxy Watch (SM-R800), and the list of features the developer claims to have working is surprisingly extensive.

title: The iPhone 18 Pro tempted me for weeks, but the Galaxy S26 Ultra wins where it counts
summary: The iPhone nearly ruined my loyalty.
body: I’ve been using the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra for nine months now, and it’s safe to say I’ve grown quite fond of it. It’s become a phone I enjoy using daily, even though I wish Samsung had done a few things differently. And at a whopping $1,400, it certainly isn’t cheap, either. So, when Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro for just $200 less, I was curious to see how the two would compare in everyday use. After all, these are two very different phones. So, I started using them side by side, putting them through everything I normally do throughout the day. And after spending enough time, I noticed something interesting: no matter which phone I was using, I kept wanting to go back to the other one. Sometimes, smaller really is better

title: Dev behind top PS3 emulator on Android releases ARMFlash, bringing tons of Flash games to Android
summary: ARMFlash brings over 200,000 Flash, HTML 5, Shockwave, Java, and PopCap titles to Android.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A key developer behind the ARMSX2 and ARMSX3 emulators has released ARMFlash on Android. This app is a port of the Flashpoint Archive project and lets you play over 200,000 web-based games and experiences on Android. ARMFlash supports both touch and controller input, while system requirements are very modest. We’ve seen a few apps that let you play Flash games on Android in recent times, most notably Swiff. Now, one of the key developers behind the ARMSX2 and ARMSX3 emulators has released ARMFlash. ARMFlash was released on GitHub yesterday (November 23) by developer jpolo1224, allowing you to play Flash, HTML 5, Shockwave, Java, and PopCap games on Android. ARMFlash is actually a port of the Flashpoint Archive project for PCs, which has saved over 200,000 old web-based games, animations, and interactive experiences.

title: The best Android keyboard app isn’t on the Play Store. Here’s how to install it
summary: HeliBoard brings customization, clipboard history and offline typing to Android, without Google’s data collection.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority Android’s always been the go-to destination when it comes to customisation and dialing in the experience exactly as you want it, and that extends to switching out the keyboard for something a bit more bespoke. For the longest time, finding a good keyboard for Android usually meant choosing between Gboard and SwiftKey . Both are excellent at predicting what you’re going to type, correcting spelling mistakes and letting you swipe between letters. The catch is that both these keyboards are made by mega corps, Google and Microsoft, and data collection is part and parcel of the deal. That’s why I’ve been looking at HeliBoard. It’s a free, open-source keyboard that offers many of the same features you’d expect from a modern Android keyboard without needing an internet connection, and, most importantly, no data collection. There are no advertisements, no cloud-based processing and plenty of customization options as is to be expected with open-source apps. There’s just one catch, you won’t find the app on the Google Play Store.

title: Google Chrome is working on 3 new filters to narrow down your browsing history
summary: You should soon be able to filter browsing history by device, date, and ‘who browsed.’
body: TL;DR Google is working on three new Chrome history filters that let users narrow down browsing activity by device, date, and who browsed. The Who browsed filter separates websites visited by users from those accessed by Gemini. The filters have been spotted in Chrome Dev and Canary, but enabling their experimental flags doesn’t appear to activate them for everyone. Google is working on introducing new filters to help you sift through your Chrome history, and these go way more granular than you might have expected. The browser could soon get three new history search filters, and one of them could even let you swap between websites you visited yourself and those that were accessed by Gemini. The development was spotted and highlighted by X user @Leopeva64 , who even shared screenshots of the redesigned history section with the new filters visible. According to the browser tipster, the new filters are already available in the Dev and Canary versions of Chrome, suggesting that they could likely go stable sometime soon.

title: Google Meet 1080p video is no longer paywalled on the web
summary: 1080p video sending for all.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google is expanding 1080p video sending to all Meet users on the web. The higher resolution is now enabled by default on computers with 1080p cameras. Videos are transmitted in 1080p when the user’s video tile is large enough to display it. Google Meet recently made it easier for presenters to share files with participants through direct download support . It’s a quality-of-life addition that, while not necessary, is very nice to have. Continuing on that trend, Google is now expanding full HD video sending to more users. While Google Meet offers 1080p video sending on the web, the feature was limited to select paid users. The important word there is “was,” as that is no longer the case. Google has announced that it is now expanding access to 1080p video sending on the web to all Meet users.

title: Gemini could soon let you archive old chats instead of deleting them
summary: Making cluttered histories a thing of the past.
body: TL;DR Google is working on a chat archiving feature for Gemini that would let users hide conversations without deleting them. Archived chats will remain accessible through the Archived filter in Gemini’s sidebar, making them easy to revisit. Google is also experimenting with a Spaces feature, but its purpose remains unclear. Google could soon let you declutter Gemini ‘s chat history by giving you the option to archive conversations. This should prevent the need to delete old conversations that you don’t want showing up within the app’s history menu. Think of this as a hide button for chats that you don’t want to delete, but don’t want to keep within view either.

title: Kodak’s SlideTag is a Find Hub tracker that doubles as a tiny E-Ink photo frame
summary: Kodak’s SlideTag blends retro charm with Bluetooth item tracking.
body: Credit: Kodak TL;DR Reto Production has launched the Kodak SlideTag for $34.99. The device is a tracker with a built-in six-color E-Ink display, and it’s capable of storing up to 12 photos. The Kodak SlideTag works with both Google’s Find Hub and Apple’s Find My networks. Just as Amazon and other online retailers have started taking orders for Motorola’s unannounced Moto Tag 3 , another brand is throwing its hat into the Bluetooth tracker ring. Reto Productions, the company behind the Kodak Charmera keychain camera, is launching its own take on the technology. This new tracker features a unique twist you won’t find on other trackers. Called the Kodak SlideTag, the design is based on the iconic 1935 Kodachrome slide mount. In addition to working with both Google’s Find Hub and Apple’s Find My networks, it features a built-in six-color E-Ink display. This display measures 1.54 inches and offers a resolution of 240 x 240 pixels.

title: YouTube introduces a new mute button on mobile, but not everyone is happy
summary: Users keep pressing by accident.
body: TL;DR YouTube is rolling out a dedicated mute button within its mobile video player, letting users silence videos without adjusting their device’s volume. Some users are frustrated by the button’s placement, reporting accidental presses when trying to skip forward in videos. The feature appears to be rolling out gradually. We have it on iOS, but not on Android. YouTube is finally giving users on its mobile apps an easier way to outright silence video without having to fiddle with their device’s volume controls, and it’s manifesting in the form of a dedicated mute button . Although the new button does sound like a welcome addition, many users are already finding the change frustrating , mainly because of accidental presses. The quality-of-life change doesn’t appear to be entirely new. We found a Reddit post from early October highlighting the mute button, suggesting that the streaming giant has been experimenting with it since then, at the very least. However, more recent reports indicate that the button is now making its way to a lot more users simultaneously (thanks @GreenShades9 ).

summary: It could make it easier for users to start a Safety Check timer.
body: TL;DR Google is working on a Safety Check integration for Google Messages. Google has been adding safety-related features to the Google Messages app over the past few months. It recently gained real-time location-sharing support , and now it seems Google is working on another safety feature. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. While digging through the latest beta of the Google Messages app (v20261116), we spotted Google working on integrating its Safety Check feature into the Messages app. In an earlier version of the app, we spotted icons related to Safety Check, and now we’re finally seeing more evidence of the feature.
